messages:
yara: heads-up 1 i'm drafting a short 'scale-policy backcompat FAQ' for Dedicated docs. aim: one compact FAQ + three tiny snippets (CLI dry-run, terraform replace, Rust SDK example) and a quick CI lint to catch legacy enums.

kevin: nice. please include a short explanation of why 'legacy' silently rejected in API v2 and the concrete mapping customers should use. that's our top support loop.

yara: will do. adding mapping note: legacy -> balanced, legacy_high -> throughput_high, legacy_saver -> cost_saver. also a short sentence about validation: "API v2 enforces enum names strictly; older TF modules that still emit legacy will be rejected at plan/apply time unless mapped."

lin: add a one-liner CI pre-apply check so infra repos fail fast. show a simple grep and also a tiny jq check for JSON-formatted templates.

yara: CI examples added:
```sh
# grep check (bash)
if grep -R "scale_policy:\s*legacy" --quiet; then
  echo "ERROR: legacy scale_policy detected. Run `tf-migrate-autoscale` or update to balanced/throughput/cost_saver"
  exit 1
fi

# JSON template check (jq)
jq -e '.autoscale.policy | test("legacy")' mypool.json && { echo "ERROR: legacy enum in JSON"; exit 1; } || true
```

kevin: wonderful. for terraform add a tiny sed/awk snippet teams can run to patch files in place for bulk migrations. saves a lot of manual toil.

yara: quick sed migration snippet:
```sh
# quick in-place mapping (backup your files!)
sed -i.bak -E 's/scale_policy\s*=\s*"legacy_high"/scale_policy = "throughput_high"/g; s/scale_policy\s*=\s*"legacy_saver"/scale_policy = "cost_saver"/g; s/scale_policy\s*=\s*"legacy"/scale_policy = "balanced"/g' **/*.tf
```

lin: add an explicit "what to test after migration" checklist: tf plan, dry-run CLI, smoke requests to dedicated model, and check billing preview. short bullets.

yara: adding 4-step post-migrate quick test: 1) `terraform plan` clean, 2) `rwdctl reserved create --dry-run` preview, 3) send 10 sample requests to the dedicated variant and assert p95, 4) review cost estimate in console.

kevin: docs folks also asked for a Rust SDK snippet 1 uncommon but helpful. can we add a tiny example showing selecting a dedicated model variant and routing hint? 3-4 lines.

yara: draft Rust snippet:
```rust
// rust snippet: prefer dedicated route
let client = redwood::Client::new(std::env::var("RWD_KEY").unwrap());
let resp = client.generate(&redwood::GenerateRequest{ model: "redwood-dedicated/gptx-dedicated-v1".into(), input: "hi".into(), routing: Some([("tier","dedicated")].iter().cloned().collect()) }).await?;
println!("{}", resp.output);
```

lin: add a short caution paragraph about isolation decorators: they can shift traffic to reserved capacity and adjust SLA/latency characteristics. advise contacting CSM and marking the change in runbooks.

yara: added caution: "Enabling isolation decorators may route traffic to reserved pools and change latency SLOs; coordinate with CSM and ops before enabling in prod." and a tiny YAML example showing the annotation key.

kevin: link hygiene: current handbook link points to an internal spreadsheet for quota tiers. replace with `/docs/dedicated/quota` and put a parenthetical about internal breakdown for partners.

yara: done. also adding a short "FAQ: silent rejection" section explaining common error messages and a `rwdctl` command to surface policy validation errors: `rwdctl validate pool --file pool.tf`.

doc-ci: PR opened by yara: https://git.redwood.internal/r/redwood/docs/+/5512 :eyes:

ops-bot: quick reminder: include a changelog fragment for the docs release and run site-lint.

kevin: i'll review the text and the Rust formatting. if that looks good i'll approve. keep the page tight.

yara: thanks all 1 will iterate and merge after green linter and one approval. will ping when live. :shipit:
